newsitem.title: USA: Mobil key tags speed up gas purchases.
newsitem.headline: Mobil key tags speed up gas purchases.

text.p: Mobil Corp. Wednesday introduced a miniature electronic device that allows consumers to buy gasoline without even having to open their wallet.

A driver simply has to wave the device, which is attached to a key chain, at the pump to turn it on. The purchase is automatically charged to a credit card that the customer has chosen in an application form.

The so-called "Speedpass" key tags contain small radio-like devices which are programmed with an identification number. When the pump is activated, the electronic system contacts Mobil to verify current credit information and charge the customer's designated credit card.
The customer's credit card number remains outside the Speedpass signal system, maintaining the confidentiality of that information.
"Our research tells us that customers are looking for the fastest and easiest way to fill up," said Brian Baker, Mobil chief operating officer for North America Marketing and Refining.
"With Speedpass we've removed the steps of finding a credit card, inserting it into the pump (and) waiting for credit card authorisation."
Mobil said it has conducted a six-month trial of the system in St. Louis, and will introduce it in its key markets nationwide this year, initially providing 1 million key tags.
Mobil sells gasoline in 28 states and Washington.
Mobil's stock edged up 12.5 cents to $131.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
